propositions: A single monolithic test iterating over 884 corpus units and spawning ~1768 pandoc processes exceeds the 300s per-test timeout on contended macOS runners, causing pytest-timeout's thread method to kill the xdist worker with os._exit(1) rather than fail the test gracefully.
The test's cost is load-dependent: measured 91.6s idle but 504.8s under saturating CPU pressure (1.7x the 300s guard), making it structurally vulnerable to macOS runner contention.
Chunking the equivalence test into fixed-size batches (constant _EQUIVALENCE_CHUNK=40) bounds per-test cost by construction, preventing corpus growth from re-crossing the timeout threshold.
All 884 renderable units remain compared byte-for-byte against the oracle with real pandoc at stride 1, preserving the equivalence property the test protects.
A coverage guard test asserts that all chunks reassemble to exactly _renderable_units() with count >= 100, ensuring no units are silently dropped by parametrization.
Chunked failure messages carry the global corpus index, enabling future failures to name which unit moved.
